items.text: By comparing patient experiences with genetic versus non-genetic results and different genetic results, it establishes patient-defined concern thresholds and support needs, avoiding the presupposition that all genetic/negative results are homogeneous.
It connects empirical ethical analysis with iterative UCD, delivering actionable Points to Consider and six to eight prototypes, rather than merely listing principles.

It incorporates non-users and users, Epic-compatible and blue-sky designs into formative research, identifying usability and equity needs, and providing a foundation for subsequent clinical validation.

The needs discovery phase only involves existing portal users, with non-users entering only at prototype testing; the single-site English setting and limited heterogeneous result categories restrict the coverage and transferability of needs.

Preferences and simulated task usability differ from safety understanding/clinical outcomes, so it cannot be concluded that electronic return can replace counseling; evaluation must adhere to clear formative boundaries.

High problem discovery rates cannot be unconditionally accumulated across prototypes, populations, or modified versions; in practice, there are very few users per prototype per round per type, and sequential development with iterative analysis also makes two-year delivery dependent.
